requirements.text: A transfer succeeds only when txid is new, source and target are distinct existing accounts, amount is positive, and source has sufficient funds; rejection returns False and changes nothing.
A successful transfer atomically debits source, credits target, records the exact (source, target, amount) fingerprint for txid, and returns True.
Repeating a successful txid with the identical fingerprint is idempotent: return True without changing balances again.
Reusing a successful txid with a different source, target, or amount raises ValueError and changes nothing.

requirements.text: Each key has an integer revision starting at zero; every put or delete advances only that key's revision exactly once, including deleting an absent key.
read(key) caches both the current revision and value, including a missing value of None, and reuses the cached value only while its cached revision equals the current key revision.
A put or delete becomes visible on the next read of that key without disturbing valid cached entries for other keys.

requirements.text: begin() returns a stable dict with exactly store, version, values, and key_versions; store is an opaque identity owned by that SnapshotMap and both nested mappings are copies.
commit(snapshot, writes) accepts only a well-formed snapshot from the same map and a dict of writes; malformed or foreign input returns False without mutation.
Conflict detection is per written key: reject the entire commit if any written key changed since snapshot, while disjoint writes from concurrent snapshots may both succeed.
A successful commit advances the global version once, stamps every written key with that new version, treats None as deletion, and changes no key outside writes.

requirements.text: reserve(keys, owner, now, ttl) requires positive ttl and unique keys; invalid input raises ValueError before changing state.
Reservation is atomic: if any key has an unexpired reservation by another owner, return None and change no reservation or token counter.
An unexpired same-owner reservation is idempotent for that key: preserve and return its existing token without extending expiry.
Every free, released, or expired key receives a new token strictly larger than every prior token for that key and expiry now + ttl; return one token per requested key.
release succeeds only for the exact current owner and token and otherwise changes nothing.
